questions.q: A user types the correct web address but is taken to a fake website that steals their login details. This attack is called
questions.why: Pharming redirects users to a fake site even when they type the correct address. Phishing uses fake messages.

questions.q: Which of these describes open-source software?
options: It is free to try but you must pay after a trial period
The source code is available to view, modify and share
It can be copied but not changed
It is sold with a licence and the code is kept secret
questions.why: Open-source software makes its source code freely available so users can view, change and share it.

questions.q: Which action is an example of ethical hacking?
options: Reading a friend's messages without asking
A company paying an expert to try to break into its network to find weaknesses
Sending a worm across a network
questions.why: Ethical hacking is authorised: the aim is to find and fix weaknesses, not to cause harm.

questions.q: Describe two ways in which technology can have a negative impact on the environment.
questions.model: Data centres and devices use large amounts of electricity, which produces carbon emissions if generated from fossil fuels. Discarded devices create e-waste containing toxic materials that can pollute land and water.
points: e-waste / toxic materials / use of finite resources
